AN UNBREAKABLE RULE OF CRYPTO HAS JUST BROKEN

Open thread • Replies: 22 • Updated: 2026-08-21 05:18 UTC

OP

But which one?

> Unbreakable Rule 1: Breaking out from the 1D 200sma after a bear market starts the next bull run

> Unbreakable Rule 2: The 4 year cycle. If this is the start of the next bullrun, that means the bottom was 58k two months ago. And that would mean that the bear market was only 6 months long, when it was supposed to be about 12.

These rules are incompatible at such an early month, so one of them is failing right now. We are in uncharted waters.

NOTES
Last cycle we saw another 'unbreakable' rule break: the bear market crashing below the weekly 200sma.

I think the 1D 200sma is the "weaker" rule, and more likely to break.

The 1D 200sma breakout, if we don't crash, leads to a golden cross about a month later. I can ignore the 1D 200sma but I would not fuck with the golden cross.

FRONTRUNNING
Everyone is now aware of the 4 year cycle, and trading accordingly. This causes 'frontrunning', which accelerates and potentially breaks the cycle.

But we have seen this once before. In early 2024 everyone tried to frontrun the bull market, which resulted in BTC passing the previous ATH way too early. People were calling for an immediate bull market peak and saying that the 4 year cycle was broken. But the 4 year cycle was stronger than the masses. BTC crabbed for an entire year, resetting the schedule of the cycle back to normal.

I think it's likely we see the same thing happen here, and we crab/dump into octoBEAR as originally planned. But if we can hold these prices until a golden cross happens, I'd bet on that most of all.

The thing is it is possible to get a mortgage without a credit score, but it requires quite a lot of shopping around. You need to find a bank/CU willing to do "manual underwriting", which is the way creditworthiness was determined prior to credit bureaus. This process actually happens in all mortgages eventually, but without a credit score, you are asking lenders to put in all that legwork at the very start of the process, when it is possible that you're just shopping rates and will bail on them in a week. This makes most large firms refuse to do it, so your best bet is a smaller credit union in your town.

Your rate will be higher than their average and you will be treated as a risky loan. However, you will build credit after a few years of payments and may be able to refi a better deal. Interestingly, since you probably don't carry any other debt your debt to income ratio will be low even with a large mortgage payment, so they may actually authorize a bigger loan than you expect.

You will need a couple years of tax records, proof of income/employment, proof of liquid assets (to show you have a down payment), several pay stubs, records of regular on time payments for rent/utilities/cars/anything. Be prepared to show where any non-employment deposits of over $300 came from.

Also, if you have a shitty score (rather than having no score / unscoreable) the bank will have to use that, and may not go through the manual process at all.

Why aren't you preserving wealth in non-depreciating asset-class goods, rather than wasting money on disposables, /biz/?

Open thread • Replies: 63 • Updated: 2026-08-20 17:09 UTC

OP

Why aren't you preserving wealth in non-depreciating asset-class goods, rather than wasting money on disposables, /biz/?

This Eames chair can be had in good second hand condition for $3800. In five or ten years I can sell it for as much as I bought it for or more, adjusted for inflation. Essentially, I rent the chair for nothing. If I'd bought a cheap chair, I would've wasted hundreds of dollars. The cheap chair cost me more than the expensive one.

Once you get out of the consumer mindset you can thinking about asset depreciation curves and TCO. Don't buy disposable junk, buy asset class investments. Buy Knoll and Eames furniture, Leica camera lenses, Rolex watches, classic hi-fi gear. Instead of being full of consumer goods depreciating to zero, my house becomes a storehouse of beautiful assets with lasting value which I can enjoy and liquidate any time I want.
